calls.head: The Islanders roll four lines, the Jets lean on their top six
calls.body: On depth, the Islanders are the league’s best, but Winnipeg is near the bottom. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.
calls.call: The Islanders spread their forward ice time deeper down the lineup than the Jets.

calls.head: Where the Islanders have the edge: shots from defensemen
calls.body: The Islanders are one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and the Jets are around the middle. It’s the widest gap between these two, though not a huge one.
calls.call: The Islanders’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Jets’.

NYI.head: We leaned the Islanders’ way (57%), but Winnipeg had other ideas.

WPG.head: We had Winnipeg as slight underdogs (43%), and they pulled it off.

surprises.head: Winnipeg hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Winnipeg’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 36, against their usual 97 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 70 games.

surprises.head: Winnipeg got the good looks
surprises.body: The Islanders usually allow more dangerous shots than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: Winnipeg’s shots at 5-on-5 had a 9.2% chance of scoring on the average shot, against their usual 6.3% (about 6.5% against the Islanders) and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far about once every 30 games.

story.head: Connor has two goals and an assist as the Jets beat the Islanders
paras: Kyle Connor got the scoring started for the Jets late in the first. Gabriel Vilardi extended the lead to 2-0 early in the second, and that one stood up as the winner. Connor scored again on the power play late in the period to make it 3-0. Logan Stanley scored his first goal for the Islanders early in the third to get the Islanders on the board. Connor added an assist for a three-point night.

The Jets drove the play, outshooting the Islanders 37-27, and the scoreboard caught up. Stuart Skinner made 26 saves for the Jets, and Semyon Varlamov kept the Islanders in it, stopping 34 of 37. The Jets improved to 14-9-4, fifth in the Central, while the Isles dropped to 12-8-5, third in the Metropolitan.

items.text: Three straight wins for the Jets.
